an4.3:1.1: “Bhikkhus, possessing four qualities, the foolish, incompetent, bad person maintains himself in a maimed and injured condition; he is blameworthy and subject to reproach by the wise; and he generates much demerit.
an4.3:1.3: (1) “Without investigating and scrutinizing, he speaks praise of one who deserves dispraise.
an4.3:1.4: (2) Without investigating and scrutinizing, he speaks dispraise of one who deserves praise.
an4.3:1.5: (3) Without investigating and scrutinizing, he believes a matter that merits suspicion.
an4.3:1.6: (4) Without investigating and scrutinizing, he is suspicious about a matter that merits belief.
an4.3:1.7: Possessing these four qualities, the foolish, incompetent, bad person maintains himself in a maimed and injured condition; he is blameworthy and subject to reproach by the wise; and he generates much demerit.
an4.3:2.1: “Bhikkhus, possessing four qualities, the wise, competent, good person preserves himself unmaimed and uninjured; he is blameless and beyond reproach by the wise; and he generates much merit.
an4.3:2.3: (1) “Having investigated and scrutinized, he speaks dispraise of one who deserves dispraise.
an4.3:2.4: (2) Having investigated and scrutinized, he speaks praise of one who deserves praise.
an4.3:2.5: (3) Having investigated and scrutinized, he is suspicious about a matter that merits suspicion.
an4.3:2.6: (4) Having investigated and scrutinized, he believes a matter that merits belief.
an4.3:2.7: Possessing these four qualities, the wise, competent, good person preserves himself unmaimed and uninjured; he is blameless and beyond reproach by the wise; and he generates much merit.”
an4.3:3.1: He who praises one deserving blame,
an4.3:3.3: casts with his mouth an unlucky throw
an4.3:3.4: by which he finds no happiness.
an4.3:4.1: Slight is the unlucky throw at dice
an4.3:4.2: that results in the loss of one’s wealth,
an4.3:4.3: the loss of all, oneself included;
an4.3:4.4: much worse is this unlucky throw
an4.3:4.5: of harboring hate against the fortunate ones.
an4.3:5.1:
For a hundred thousand and thirty-six
nirabbudas, plus five abbudas,
an4.3:5.3: the slanderer of noble ones goes to hell,
an4.3:5.4: having defamed them with evil speech and mind.
